minutes.headline: Committee heard hours of public comment on the cancelled Thanksgiving football game after a racist graffiti incident; no vote taken.
minutes.summary: The meeting was dominated by public comment on the superintendent's decision to cancel the Thanksgiving football game after racist graffiti was painted on a student's home. The superintendent announced a written statement and outreach to outside agencies, and the committee discussed forming a community advisory committee on tolerance and diversity. The MSBA approval of a new middle/high school project was reported and a facilities budget was briefly presented. No formal vote on the game was taken.

what_happened.line: The School Committee took no vote on the cancelled Thanksgiving football game; the chair said the superintendent's cancellation stands for now.
Public comment on the cancellation, held after a racist graffiti incident, ran for most of the meeting and drew speakers on both sides.
The chair confirmed there was no motion and no vote on the football game that night.
The superintendent reported that the MSBA board approved the new middle/high school proposal and committed funds, subject to town meeting approval.
The committee discussed an advisory committee on tolerance and diversity of about seven members, with its timeframe to be set at the next meeting.

why_it_matters: The MSBA commitment depends on a town meeting vote, so residents will be asked to approve the new middle/high school project.
The football game decision rests with the superintendent unless the committee chooses to overrule it, and the advisory committee would shape how the district responds to the incident.
A facilities budget with an increase was presented for next year, and the natural gas line is likely underfunded, so money may be moved between lines.
watch_next: The superintendent's written statement on the status of the investigations, to be released and posted online the next day.
The next committee meeting, where the advisory committee's timeframe is to be set.
